contents.text: Hurricanes form only under certain conditions. They only form over warm ocean water. The warm water evaporates and rises into the air. If there is a light wind blowing, it can push the water vapor up higher. The rising water vapor helps the storm grow in two ways. As the water vapor rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds. Also, when the water vapor goes up, it leaves space for more air to blow in. The new air helps the hurricane grow.

contents.text: Hurricanes form only under certain conditions. They only form over warm ocean water. The warm water evaporates and rises into the air. If there is a light wind blowing, it can push the water vapor up higher. The rising water vapor helps the storm grow in two ways. As the water vapor rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds. Also, when the water vapor goes up, it leaves space for more air to blow in. The new air helps the hurricane grow.

As more warm water evaporates and rises, the storm grows bigger and stronger. As the storm moves across the ocean or land, heavy rain falls from the clouds, and the wind blows faster. If the wind reaches a speed of 74 miles per hour (mph) or faster, the storm is called a hurricane.

If there is a light wind blowing, it can push the water vapor up higher. The rising water vapor helps the storm grow in two ways. As the water vapor rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds. Also, when the water vapor goes up, it leaves space for more air to blow in. The new air helps the hurricane grow.

header.text: How did Hurricane Isabel get its name?

content.text: Hurricane names are chosen from six different lists. One list is used each year. After six years, the lists are reused in the same order.

On each list, there is a name for almost every letter of the alphabet. Each list goes back and forth between male and female names. So, on one list, "A" is a female name, and "B" is a male name. On the next list, "A" is a male name, and "B" is a female name.

contents.text: Hurricanes are named in the order in which they form. The first hurricane of the year gets the first name on the list. The second hurricane gets the second name on the list. If all the names are used but there are still more hurricanes, the list starts over with "A."

content.text: Hurricane names are chosen from six different lists. One list is used each year. After six years, the lists are reused in the same order.

On each list, there is a name for almost every letter of the alphabet. Each list goes back and forth between male and female names. So, on one list, "A" is a female name, and "B" is a male name. On the next list, "A" is a male name, and "B" is a female name.

contents.text: Hurricanes are named in the order in which they form. The first hurricane of the year gets the first name on the list. The second hurricane gets the second name on the list. If all the names are used but there are still more hurricanes, the list starts over with "A."
